title: NAD+ Therapy in Brisbane: Benefits, Science, and What to Expect
html:
What Is NAD+?

Nicotinamide adenine dinucleotide (NAD+) is a coenzyme found in every living cell. It plays a central role in two of the most fundamental biological processes in the human body: energy metabolism and DNA repair.

In energy metabolism, NAD+ acts as an electron carrier in the mitochondrial respiratory chain – the process by which cells convert nutrients into ATP, the body's primary energy currency. Without adequate NAD+, this process becomes inefficient, contributing to the fatigue, cognitive decline, and reduced physical capacity that many people associate with ageing.

In DNA repair, NAD+ is consumed by enzymes called sirtuins and PARPs, which detect and repair DNA damage. These repair processes are essential for cellular longevity and cancer prevention. As NAD+ levels decline, DNA repair becomes less efficient, accelerating the cellular ageing process.

Why Do NAD+ Levels Decline With Age?

NAD+ levels in human tissue decline by approximately 50% between the ages of 40 and 60. This decline is driven by several factors:

Reduced synthesis – the body's ability to produce NAD+ from dietary precursors (tryptophan, niacin, and nicotinamide riboside) decreases with age.

Increased consumption – chronic inflammation, DNA damage, and metabolic stress all increase the demand for NAD+, depleting available stores.

Lifestyle factors – alcohol consumption, poor sleep, sedentary behaviour, and a diet low in NAD+ precursors all accelerate NAD+ depletion.

The result is a progressive energy deficit at the cellular level – contributing to fatigue, cognitive decline, reduced muscle mass, impaired immune function, and the broader constellation of changes we associate with biological ageing.

The Science Behind NAD+ Therapy

NAD+ therapy has been the subject of significant scientific interest over the past decade, driven largely by research from institutions including Harvard Medical School, the Salk Institute, and the National Institute on Ageing.

NAD+ therapy has been the subject of scientific research in relation to cellular energy metabolism, mitochondrial function, and ageing biology. The human clinical evidence is still developing. All NAD+ programs at Australian Longevity Clinic are individually assessed and prescribed by our registered medical practitioners following a thorough consultation.

Why IV NAD+ Rather Than Oral Supplements?

Oral NAD+ precursors – including nicotinamide riboside (NR) and nicotinamide mononucleotide (NMN) – are widely available as supplements and do raise NAD+ levels in the body. However, IV NAD+ infusion offers several advantages:

Direct delivery – IV infusion delivers NAD+ directly into the bloodstream, bypassing the digestive tract and achieving immediate cellular availability without the conversion steps required by oral precursors.

Higher peak levels – IV infusion achieves significantly higher peak plasma NAD+ concentrations than oral supplementation, which may be important for therapeutic applications.

Intravenous delivery – IV infusion delivers NAD+ directly into the bloodstream, bypassing gastrointestinal absorption. Individual responses vary and are not guaranteed.

Therapeutic dosing – IV infusion allows precise, high-dose delivery that is difficult to achieve reliably with oral supplements.

What to Expect From NAD+ Therapy

NAD+ therapy is individually assessed and prescribed by our registered medical practitioners. Individual responses vary, and results depend on baseline health status, lifestyle factors, and the number of infusions received. NAD+ infusion therapy is not intended to diagnose, treat, cure, or prevent any disease or medical condition. A thorough medical assessment is required before any program is prescribed.

What to Expect During a NAD+ Infusion

NAD+ infusions are administered slowly to minimise the side effects that can occur with rapid delivery. A typical NAD+ infusion at Australian Longevity Clinic takes between 2 and 4 hours, depending on the dose prescribed.

During the infusion, some patients experience transient sensations including chest tightness, nausea, flushing, or a feeling of restlessness. These effects are dose-dependent and are managed by adjusting the infusion rate. They resolve immediately when the rate is slowed and do not indicate a serious adverse reaction.

Most patients find the experience comfortable and use the time to relax, work, or read. Individual responses to NAD+ infusion vary.

How Many NAD+ Infusions Are Recommended?

For patients new to NAD+ therapy, we typically recommend an initial course of 2 to 4 infusions over 2 to 4 weeks to achieve meaningful cellular replenishment. Maintenance infusions – typically monthly or quarterly – are then used to sustain NAD+ levels over time.

The optimal protocol varies between individuals and is determined based on your health goals, baseline status, and treatment response. Our doctors will design a personalised NAD+ program as part of your overall longevity plan.
